results.snippet: # US Dollar Index (DXY). The US Dollar Index (DXY) measures the value of the US dollar relative to a basket of six major foreign currencies: Euro (57.6% weight), Japanese Yen (13.6%), British Pound (11.9%), Canadian Dollar (9.1%), Swedish Krona (4.2%), and Swiss Franc (3.6%). The DXY is critical for emerging markets like India because a strengthening dollar (rising DXY) typically leads to capital outflows from emerging markets, commodity price declines (as most commodities are USD-denominated), and currency depreciation. Traders watch the DXY as a barometer of global risk appetite and USD strength. If you had invested in US Dollar Index (DXY):. Is the US dollar index important? Everything you will need to know about the US dollar index will be right here in this article. The US Dollar Index, also known as DXY, is used to measure the value of the US dollar against a basket of six world currencies - **Euro**, Swiss Franc, **Japanese Yen**, **Canadian dollar**, **British pound**, and Swedish Krona. The value of the index is a fair indication of the dollar’s value in global markets.
